_meta.audience: High-school-age sprinters (roughly 14-18). Volumes and intensities are set toward the conservative end for developing athletes. A 400m specialist with several years of training age can tolerate more; a first-year athlete should do less. A qualified coach must individualize before use.
_meta.not_medical_or_coaching_advice: These templates are a starting structure, not a substitute for in-person coaching. They do not account for an individual's injury history, biomechanics, training age, or maturation. Anyone with pain, recent injury, or no coach supervision should not follow these unmodified.
_meta.methodology_basis: Built on widely accepted sprint-training principles: the high/low CNS-loading model (alternating high-intensity neural days with low-intensity recovery days, avoiding medium-intensity 'no man's land'); classic sprint energy-system development (acceleration -> maximum velocity -> speed endurance -> special endurance); long/full recoveries on all high-CNS work to preserve quality; extensive tempo for recovery and aerobic support on low days; and a linear-to-specific periodization (general prep -> specific prep -> pre-competition -> competition/taper). These are established coaching frameworks, not claims tied to any specific cited study. A coach should confirm the prescriptions suit the individual.

intensity_key.accel: Acceleration work, maximal intent, short distance, full recovery
intensity_key.max_velocity: Top-speed work (flying runs), maximal, full recovery
intensity_key.general_strength: Bodyweight/circuit/medball; supports without high CNS cost

_meta.scaling_note: Each phase gives one weekly microcycle plus a progression rule. The app expands the phase across its weeks using that rule, and the daily readiness engine then scales the prescribed volume by its 0.5-1.0 multiplier.
_meta.review_note: Reviewed by multiple qualified reviewers and approved for use (sign-off recorded 2026-08-08). Volumes remain set toward the conservative end for developing athletes; a coach should still individualise for injury history, training age and maturation.
coach_review_checklist: Are weekly high-CNS day counts appropriate for THIS athlete's training age? (Drafted at 3/week; a beginner may need 2.)
Are total sprint volumes per session age-appropriate and not excessive?
Are recoveries long enough to keep every rep high-quality? (Lengthen, never shorten, if in doubt.)
Does the strength work need to be reduced/supervised? (Loads intentionally left to the S&C coach.)
Does the taper length/volume drop suit the athlete's competition schedule?
Any contraindications from the athlete's injury history? (e.g. hamstring, Achilles, shin issues change speed-endurance volume.)

templates.summary: The 100m is acceleration plus max velocity, with just enough speed endurance to hold form through the line. Special endurance is minimal. Speed quality is protected above all else.

phases.name: General Preparation
phases.rationale: Build work capacity, technical base, and tissue tolerance before high-CNS speed loads. Acceleration emphasis (short distance, controlled), extensive tempo for volume without neural cost, general strength. No max-velocity work yet.
phases.progression: Add ~1 rep or ~5m to accel work each week; increase tempo volume modestly. Keep intensities the same.

blocks.name: Dynamic warm-up + drills
blocks.detail: 15-20 min: mobility, A/B skips, wall drives

blocks.name: Short accelerations
blocks.target: Maximal intent, low heel recovery, gradual rise; from 3-point start

blocks.name: General strength
blocks.detail: Medball throws + core, 15-20 min (loads per S&C coach)

blocks.name: Extensive tempo
blocks.target: <70% effort, relaxed, on grass if possible

blocks.name: Accelerations
blocks.target: Maximal, smooth transition out of drive phase

blocks.name: Strength
blocks.detail: Compound lifts, supervised; loads per S&C coach

blocks.name: Accelerations w/ varied starts
blocks.target: Maximal; mix block and standing starts

weekly_microcycle.name: Optional light mobility or full rest

phases.name: Specific Preparation
phases.rationale: Introduce maximum velocity (flying runs) and short speed endurance. This is where top-speed mechanics develop. Recoveries stay full to protect quality. Tempo maintained on low days. The highest-risk phase for hamstring strain, so volumes stay modest and recoveries generous.
phases.progression: Weeks 4-5 introduce flys at submaximal-to-maximal; weeks 6-7 add one speed-endurance rep. If any tightness, reduce volume rather than push.

blocks.name: Flying runs
blocks.target: 20m build-in, 20m max-velocity zone; maximal, relaxed face/hands

blocks.name: Short speed endurance
blocks.target: ~95%, hold mechanics; STOP if form breaks down

blocks.name: Flying runs
blocks.target: Maximal top speed, full recovery between reps

phases.name: Pre-Competition
phases.rationale: Sharpen race-specific speed. Full max-velocity quality plus speed endurance toward race distance (80-120m) to hold speed through the line. Volume trends down slightly as intensity peaks. Block starts integrated.
phases.progression: Maintain intensity at maximal; trim total volume slightly week to week so freshness rises into competition.

blocks.name: Speed endurance
blocks.target: ~95-100%, maintain top-speed mechanics deep into the run

blocks.name: Block start to max velocity
blocks.target: Full race acceleration into top speed

phases.name: Competition / Taper
phases.rationale: Drop volume sharply while keeping intensity high to peak freshness without losing speed. Short, sharp, fully-recovered work. Race days replace one or both high days.
phases.progression: Cut total volume ~40-60% vs pre-comp. Keep reps maximal but few. Insert competitions as the priority sessions.

blocks.name: Optional shakeout
blocks.detail: A few easy strides + drills, or off

blocks.name: Race
blocks.detail: Compete; if no meet, 2-3 maximal short accelerations with full recovery

templates.summary: The 200m needs top speed AND the ability to hold it through a curve and a long straight. Speed endurance and special endurance I carry more weight than in the 100m, but max velocity is still developed first.

phases.name: General Preparation
phases.rationale: Work capacity, technical base, tissue tolerance. Acceleration and extensive tempo, slightly higher tempo volume than the 100m plan to build the aerobic-support base the 200m's longer effort benefits from.
phases.progression: Add a tempo rep or accel rep each week; intensities constant.

phases.name: Specific Preparation
phases.rationale: Develop maximum velocity and begin speed endurance (60-120m) plus special endurance I (150m). The 200m athlete must learn to apply force while fatiguing. Full/long recoveries protect mechanics. Curve running introduced.
phases.progression: Lengthen speed-endurance reps toward 120m and add a special-endurance rep across the phase. Reduce if mechanics deteriorate.

blocks.name: Speed endurance
blocks.target: ~95%, hold form; stop set if mechanics break

phases.name: Pre-Competition
phases.rationale: Blend race components: top-speed quality, speed endurance, and special endurance I trending toward 180-200m so the athlete rehearses the full race demand. Volume tapers slightly.
phases.progression: Push special-endurance distance toward race distance; trim total reps; keep intensity high.

blocks.name: Special endurance
blocks.target: ~93%, run the curve-to-straight transition like the race

phases.name: Competition / Taper
phases.rationale: Reduce volume sharply, keep intensity high and fresh, prioritize racing. Short maximal speed plus one short special-endurance touch to keep race feel.
phases.progression: Cut volume ~40-60%; races become the key sessions.

blocks.name: Race
blocks.detail: Compete; if no meet, 2-3 maximal short flys, full recovery

templates.summary: The 400m is a speed-endurance event: maintaining a high percentage of top speed while heavily fatigued. It needs more special-endurance volume than the sprints, but speed must still be developed and maintained or there's nothing to endure. The classic mistake is too much hard 'medium' running and not enough true speed or true special endurance. This plan keeps the high/low separation strict to avoid that trap.

phases.name: General Preparation
phases.rationale: Build the largest aerobic and work-capacity base of the three events (the 400 has the biggest aerobic contribution of the sprints), plus acceleration and strength. Higher extensive-tempo volume. This base lets the athlete tolerate the heavy special-endurance work later.
phases.progression: Increase tempo volume each week; add accel reps; intensities constant.

phases.name: Specific Preparation
phases.rationale: Develop speed (max velocity) so there's speed to endure, and begin special endurance I (150-300m). Maintain tempo. The high/low pattern is critical here: true speed days and true special-endurance days, with genuine recovery between, NOT a smear of hard medium running.
phases.progression: Lengthen special-endurance reps toward 300m; keep recoveries full. Maintain one true speed day weekly so top speed doesn't erode.

blocks.name: Flying runs
blocks.target: Maximal; keep the 400 runner's speed alive

blocks.name: Speed endurance
blocks.target: ~95%, hold mechanics deep into the run

phases.name: Pre-Competition
phases.rationale: The defining 400m phase: special endurance II (300-500m or broken runs) to build the ability to hold speed through the final 100m, while protecting top speed with a short maximal touch. This is where the '300m wall' is trained. Volumes are high-quality and recoveries are full; this phase is demanding, so the readiness engine's scaling matters most here.
phases.progression: Build special-endurance II toward and slightly beyond race distance (e.g. 300m -> 350m, or broken 500s); keep total reps low and recoveries long. Reduce on low-readiness days.

blocks.name: Special endurance II
blocks.target: ~90-93%, even split, train the last-100m hold; can be run as a broken rep (e.g. 300m, or 200m+200m with 45s) per coach

phases.name: Competition / Taper
phases.rationale: Sharpen and freshen. Sharply reduced volume, intensity preserved. Keep one short special-endurance touch for race feel and one short speed touch; prioritize competition. The 400 takes longer to recover from than the short sprints, so spacing around races is generous.
phases.progression: Cut volume ~50%; races are the priority sessions; ensure 2+ easy/rest days around each race.

blocks.name: Race
blocks.detail: Compete; if no meet, 1x200m special endurance at ~92%, full recovery
